text:
sofia_sales: Tideway exec demo prep — they're hitting slow first-token (median ~2.2s, p95 ~5.3s) and sporadic 429s during our prefill step. Their load generator spikes to ~140rps for 45s. Need an ops quick fix and a clear ask for the customer before the demo. @ben_platform @rahul_infra

ben_platform: Thanks. Confirm hosted route and model? Any client flags (prefill, prefer_single, session_id)?

sofia_sales: Hosted. route=default-prod/tideway, model=rw-13b-v2-int8. Clients use prefill=true, session_id=random (they spawn new session per user), max_tokens=600. Not setting prefer_single. Attached small log snippet:

```
[2026-03-22T08:12:03Z] shard=17 batcher: queued=24
[2026-03-22T08:12:03Z] batcher: emitted batch_size=2 (queue_time=240ms)
[2026-03-22T08:12:04Z] handler: compute_start model=rw-13b-v2-int8
[2026-03-22T08:12:04Z] kv: miss key=session_xyz
[2026-03-22T08:12:05Z] handler: first_token=2.4s
[2026-03-22T08:12:05Z] limiter: action=reject reason=circuit_breaker -> 429
```

rahul_infra: Two signals: (A) really small batch_size during the spike (batch_size p50=2) + long queue_time -> inefficient kernels launching more frequently; (B) KV miss rate is high because of random session_ids. Also limiter firing is a circuit_breaker due to temporary shard saturation. Need metrics: batch_size histogram, queue_time percentiles, kv_hit_rate, and shard.cpu_util.

sofia_sales: Metrics for the 08:12 window: batch_size p50=2 p95=8, queue_time p95=220ms, kv_hit_rate=18%, shard_cpu=92%, limiter.rejects=45 (circuit_breaker).

ben_platform: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) throttle client ramp to ~35rps during demo, 2) canary route config: batch_window_ms=60, min_batch_size=6, enable session_pooling=true (server side keepalive sessions to reuse kv cache), 3) add short backoff on prefill path so bursts don't trigger circuit. I'll open a canary for default-prod/tideway.

eva_compliance: Quick note: they also asked about log retention for prefill messages and whether prefill contents land in analytics. Hosted defaults are 7d retention; we can suppress request body logging for this customer if they want. Also confirm whether prefills include PII — if so, recommend masking on client side or opt into PII redaction.

sofia_sales: They'll opt for masking. Back to canary.

deploy_bot: Canary rollout started for default-prod/tideway with changes: batch_window_ms=60, min_batch_size=6, session_pooling=true, backoff_policy=exponential-50ms, job_id=c7d9.

ben_platform: After 5m canary: batch_size p50->6, p95->10; queue_time p95->95ms; shard_cpu->68%; kv_hit_rate->42% (session_pooling helped). First-token p50 improved 2.2s->1.0s, p95 improved 5.3s->1.8s. No 429s observed during the canary window.

rahul_infra: Nice. Longer-term asks: - Add a small persistent warmup pool that establishes sessions and pins prefixes to shards (reduces KV miss rate). - Consider route-level prefill_concurrency_limit to smooth bursts. - For high-demo bursts, offer a temporary shard scale-out or burst_credit to avoid circuit_breaker.

ben_platform: Also adding a short runbook blurb: "If demo prefill causes TTFT spikes: throttle client ramp to <=40rps, enable session_pooling, set min_batch_size>=6 and batch_window_ms>=50-60ms, and run a 2min warmup job that reuses session_ids."

sofia_sales: I'll tell Tideway to throttle ramp to 30-35rps and run a 2-minute warmup that reuses session_ids. I'll also send along the compliance masking guidance.

eva_compliance: Received questionnaire. Will draft PII handling response and confirm suppression of request-body logs if they want it.

deploy_bot: Canary completed successfully. Rolling changes to full route default-prod/tideway 	9:05 UTC job_id=c7d9 -> deployed.

ben_platform: Rolling to full route now. I'll monitor the next demo run. If anything resurfaces we'll temporarily scale shard count.

sofia_sales: Thanks team 389 — demo scheduled in 45m. I'll update Tideway and include the warmup checklist and brief pricing note that warmups increase token usage (we can discuss Dedicated/reserved capacity for stable demo pricing).
